title: A Echo for the Vector Again
premise: Jude Whitlock, sole navigator of the derelict relay station Vesper, keeps the beacon burning and avoids the cryo-hold where forty-one backups of herself sleep — copies made during a war she helped end and was ordered to forget. When a ghost ship appears on her scopes carrying a manifest with the name of a man she buried, Jude learns the beacon is not a navigation aid but a dead-man's switch: a message that can either expose the armistice as fraud or detonate the ceasefire for good. Hunted by both fleets' cleanup crews and shadowed by an awakened backup who remembers what Jude chose to forget, she must carry the message through contested space to the one living witness. In the end Jude sacrifices her own continuity — letting her backup, who loves differently and remembers more, deliver the truth — buying peace at the price of never being the woman who survives to see it.
about_author: Mara Joubert is a former maritime cartographer from Cape Town who turned to science fiction after a decade charting waters that no longer exist. She writes about people who maintain things — beacons, lighthouses, memories — long after everyone else has moved on.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes daily life aboard station Vesper: calibrating the beacon, logging empty traffic, avoiding the cryo-hold's humming door. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Forty-One Sleepers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Maintenance takes her past the hold; she counts the pods without opening them. A nightmare fragment surfaces — a launch bay, screaming metal. Beat: guilt she cannot source.

chapters.title: Traffic That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The beacon pings a return signal from a ship class decommissioned six years ago. She logs it as debris. Beat: first crack in her carefully maintained denial.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Jude decrypts the ghost ship's transponder out of boredom and finds the name Elias Vance — the man whose funeral she attended, or thinks she did. Beat: vertigo; the past is not where she left it.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: POV: Renn Okafor, a fleet auditor arriving under friendly pretenses. He asks oddly precise questions about the beacon's commissioning date. Beat: polite menace; Jude realizes she is being measured.

chapters.title: What the Manual Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She pulls the beacon's original schematics and finds a second transmission layer, encrypted in her own handwriting style. Beat: dawning horror that she built the thing she fears.

chapters.title: The Hold Opens
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Power fluctuation forces her into the cryo-hold. One pod reads ACTIVE. She runs. Beat: terror; the past has started waking up without permission.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's POV. The war's final year: Elias Vance, comms officer, her lover, and the mission they flew together that she cannot fully recall. Beat: tenderness braided with dread.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Corridor
chapters.summary: Jude confronts the awakened backup — who calls herself Wren and claims to remember everything Jude forgot. Beat: uncanny confrontation; meeting your own unfinished grief.

chapters.title: Two of Everything
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She explains the backup program: navigators copied before suicide runs, memories selectively redacted after. Jude's erasure was ordered, not chosen. Beat: betrayal reframes her whole life.

chapters.title: Auditor's Gambit
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. He reports to his handler that the beacon is live and the subject unstable; authorization comes back: terminate and scuttle. Beat: cold machinery of institutional memory control.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren decode the beacon's hidden payload together: proof the armistice was signed by a fabricated command authority — the war never legally ended. Beat: the stakes crystallize; delivering this ends or restarts everything.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Someone vents the station's atmosphere controls. Wren saves her, but the beacon's transmitter is damaged. Beat: survival at cost; they must leave to finish the job.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They strip the ghost ship — Elias's old vessel, impossibly intact — for the run to Ceres Station, where the last witness lives. Beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Silent-running through the debris fields; the two women navigate by memory and argument, their identical instincts diverging. Beat: intimacy between strangers who share a skull.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Meridian
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A fleet checkpoint; Renn is aboard the inspection ship. Wren poses as Jude while Jude hides in a cargo pod. Beat: identity as performance; she watches herself lie well.

chapters.title: What I Chose
chapters.summary: Flashback, Wren's POV. The suicide run at Kalder's Reach: Wren volunteered, Jude refused, and the copy was made anyway. Beat: the sisters' wound revealed — each believes she abandoned the other.

chapters.title: Ceres
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ceres Station's black-market sprawl; they find the witness, Admiral Sefa Idris, retired and dying. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Witness Refuses
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. She knows the message is true but releasing it means civil war among the colonies; she'd rather die with the lie. Beat: despair; truth alone convinces no one.

chapters.title: Renn Closes In
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. His strike team reaches Ceres; he hesitates when he sees Jude's file includes a termination order predating the war's end. Beat: the instrument begins doubting the hand.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Underlevels
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude trades the only copy of her own backup codes to a syndicate broker for safe passage and a broadcast window. Beat: sacrifice; she pays in futures, not credits.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Docks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Strike team hits the docks; Idris is killed covering their escape, pressing her seal ring into Wren's hand. Beat: grief weaponized; now they carry a martyr's authority.

chapters.title: Split Course
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Two fleet nets are converging; the broadcast window exists on opposite sides of the system. They must split up — each taking half the authentication chain. Beat: dread of separation; neither trusts the other to survive.

chapters.title: Alone With Myself
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Solo flight, quiet chapter. She finally opens her own redacted memories via the ship's medical suite and remembers choosing to forget — to survive the guilt of surviving Elias. Beat: catharsis; the price of survival named.

chapters.title: Wren's War
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Running the inner-system gauntlet, Wren realizes she doesn't want to deliver the message — she wants to burn the fleet that made her. Beat: dark mirror; love against duty pulling her toward vengeance.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. He catches Wren's ship but lets her go, transmitting instead a warning to Jude: the fleet plans to scuttle the whole relay network, burying the evidence forever. Beat: defection; the auditor chooses memory over orders.

chapters.title: The Second Ghost Ship
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She finds a second vessel from the phantom manifest — crewed by other redacted backups, alive and hiding for years. Beat: she was never the only one; community of the erased.

chapters.title: Council of Copies
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The backups debate: broadcast the truth and risk war, or stay hidden forever. Jude argues for delivery; Wren, arriving battered, argues for fire. Beat: the theme argued in the flesh.

chapters.title: Reconciliation
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren, private scene. They finally speak the Kalder's Reach truth to each other; forgiveness, imperfect but real. Beat: love against duty resolved between the two halves of one woman.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The broker's broadcast window activates — eleven minutes, one antenna, both fleets listening. Beat: ticking clock at maximum compression.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The transmission begins; authentication chains interlock across two ships. Fleet jammers claw at the signal. Beat: white-knuckle tension.

chapters.title: Jamming
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The inner-system leg fails; Wren flies her ship directly into the jammer array to clear the line. Beat: the vengeance arc redeemed into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The full message lands on every open channel: the fraudulent armistice, Idris's seal, the backup program's existence. Both fleets go silent. Beat: the world holding its breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath, First Hour
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Fleets stand down amid chaos; some commanders move to comply, others to coup. Renn releases his own records, tipping the balance toward disclosure. Beat: fragile pivot toward peace.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wren's ship is lost with all hands — including, the logs say, Wren. Jude grieves herself. Beat: the cost made personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Hearing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A tribunal summons her as living evidence; she testifies beside the surviving backups, refusing to let them be classified as property. Beat: dignity reclaimed for the erased.

chapters.title: Decommissioning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She returns to Vesper to shut down the beacon properly — and finds Wren's escape pod logged, weeks old, drifting. Beat: grief interrupted by impossible hope.

chapters.title: Recovery
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, damaged and partial. She survived in a crippled pod, redacted again by hypoxia, remembering only that she was loved. Beat: tender inversion — now Wren must be told who she is.

chapters.title: A Echo for the Vector Again
chapters.summary: Both POV. Jude re-teaches Wren their shared history, choosing which memories to give back and which to let rest. The beacon burns on, repurposed as a memorial channel. Beat: quiet grace; memory as gift rather than wound.

chapters.title: Course Set
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, closing. The two women take a new contract escorting refugee ships through the old war lanes. The war stays ended because people keep telling the truth about it. Beat: earned peace; love and duty finally pointing the same direction.
